stories.completionNotes: commit 7c02b16. MERGE: dashboard.html gains data-states (PLURAL) naming all three state files; tick() fetches each through a NEW per-tick `stateOnce` cache and renders a section per source via healthCardView/renderHealthCard. The standalone Battery Health, Light and LTFT Trend slots are gone from the DOM/nav. INDEPENDENCE is the load-bearing property: availability resolves PER SECTION, never per card -- routed through one card-level check, a dead UPS would blank the two live instruments beside it, a fabricated 'nothing is readable' built out of one real fault. THE GATE SPEAKS INSTEAD OF HIDING: a standalone card could be `hidden`, but a section inside an always-visible card cannot vanish without leaving a hole, so fuel trim renders the words 'no engine data'; the gate is evaluated BEFORE the data and a gated section carries NO view at all, so a stale ltft-trend file from the last drive cannot paint a trim for an engine that is not running. Ships data-gated="true" so the pre-first-poll window fails closed. The vocabulary now has THREE dispositions (gated / no-data / live), not two. RETITLE IS LABEL-ONLY -- emitter, thresholds, classifier and insufficient guard untouched, Spool's LTFT semantics preserved. The three renderers now take a BODY element, not a card (renderBatteryHealthBody/renderLightBody/renderLtftTrendBody): reaching for their own `.card-body` silently assumed one source per card, the assumption this card overturns. The dead ltft-trend tick branch is DELETED, not left unreachable. stories.completionNotes: commit 57e8452. RESUMED A DIED ITERATION -- the tree already carried the full US-508 implementation + a 44-test suite from a prior iteration that expired before running its gate or committing (TD-059 again, third sprint running). Per the recovery precedent I did NOT re-implement and did NOT trust it: I read the diff, ran the targeted suites (green, exit 0), then AUDITED the work against each AC rather than accepting the green. That audit found two real gaps, which are this iteration's actual contribution. GAP 1 -- ALTITUDE WAS ENTIRELY UNPINNED. The code renders it correctly via naTile and its own comment names the hazard ('a zeroed altitude renders as sea level -- a confident lie'), but NOT ONE test enforced it anywhere in tests/ui. AC-1 asks for a prominent altitude and Atlas ruled it typed-NULL/no_source; it is the one tile whose only correct rendering is an absence, and absence is the easiest thing to 'fix' by accident. Added 4 view pins + 1 DOM-wiring pin (a view key nobody paints is not a readout, and an always-NA tile is exactly what gets tidied away by someone cleaning the renderer). The strongest asserts NO DIGIT AT ALL rather than == 'NA', which also catches the helpful '0 ft'/'0 m' variants. GAP 2 -- THE RAISED BRIDGE CADENCE WAS UNPINNED. DEFAULT_STATE_HZ went 4 -> 10 (the whole AC-5 transport ruling), but every rate test in test_imu_state_bridge.py passes stateHz=4 EXPLICITLY, so the default path was never exercised -- a silent revert to 4 would leave the entire suite green while the tape and g-trail visibly stutter on the panel, a defect only a human in a moving car would ever report. Added a behavioural default-cadence test + a CROSS-ARTIFACT pin that reads the shipped carousel.js IMU_POLL_MS and asserts the producer is never slower than its consumer polls (the constant's docstring CLAIMED that grounding; a claim in a comment is not a check). Also corrected the neighbouring 4 Hz test's docstring, which asserted the old POLL_MS=250 grounding as if it were the rule. TDD ON PRE-EXISTING CODE = MUTATION PROOF: all 5 new pins passed on first run, which proves nothing, so I broke each defect they forbid (fabricate a sea-level altitude / drop the field / compute-but-never-paint it / revert the cadence to 4) and confirmed each went RED naming the right test, restoring from an in-`finally` backup so the uncommitted work could never be lost. Verified the restore by diff-stat before staging. GREEN in-loop (synchronous): tests/ui + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py + tests/pi/sensors + tests/pi/splash + tests/test_config_validator.py = 779 passed / 1 skipped, exit 0; ruff clean on all 6 touched .py; python validate_config.py passes. HOST GAPS unchanged (Sprints 64-68): make/black/mypy absent on this Windows box -- PM please run mypy at integration (imu_state_bridge.py + validator.py both changed). >>> THIS STORY CLOSES US-507'S FLAGGED VALIDATION GAP: absorbing Motion into the home slot is what reaches the locked 4 cards, so the 'US-507 alone lands at 5' criterion routed to the PM inbox is now discharged by US-507+US-508 jointly. Note test_dashboard_kit's count STAYED 4 across this change for a DIFFERENT REASON (the old idle card wore `card idle-card` and was never counted; the home slot is a plain `.card` and is) -- a bare count that survives for the wrong reason is vacuous, so the inventory test now NAMES every slot. ON-PI GATE OWED (A-16, cannot be discharged here): parked -> idle face; live states/imu -> compass tape + gear + grade + altitude; past 0.6 g -> amber; stale IMU -> falls back to idle, never frozen. WATCH: (1) the tape's SCROLL DIRECTION -- a backwards tape is a plausible instrument that is exactly wrong and no screenshot shows it; turn right, the tape must scroll left. (2) Confirm the swap does not leave a stale <svg> under the idle message. (3) states/imu is live @0x69 but the light sensor at 0x29 is UNPLUGGED -- unrelated to this card, do not read it as an IMU fault.
acceptance: re-issue the live card to the CIO-locked spec (2026-07-27-pi-live-instrument-card.md): scrolling compass TAPE under a fixed caret (NOT the built rotating-needle dial); add the GEAR glyph (Spool OBD derivation, '--' when ambiguous); AMBER at 0.6 g (not just the 1.0 g full-scale clamp); grade % + prominent altitude + ~15-min moving trend
HOME-SLOT SWAP: the home slot (position 1) shows the idle card when parked and the live instrument when driving -- one slot, two faces (not a separate always-present card)
honest fallback: stale/absent states/imu -> idle card, never a frozen motion display (states/imu is live @0x69)

[ATLAS CONTRACT RULED 2026-07-31 -- UNGATED] states/imu is the DERIVED display view produced by the ONE dedicated reader/bridge (single owner, DELTA-2); the display is a PURE consumer (never opens bus/I2C, never fuses). Fields: headingDeg 0-359 from mag TILT-COMPENSATED via accel (flag as known-limit if v1 non-compensated -- the READER owns this, not the display); gradePct=tan(pitch)*100; gLat/gLon = tilt-compensated horizontal accel in UNITS OF g; gMag=sqrt(gLat^2+gLon^2) derived-once (don't recompute in the g-circle); altitude = typed-NULL + reason:'no_source' (NO GPS/baro source today -- honest-NA, never fabricated/zeroed; field stays for zero-rework later); available(bool)+ts(fresh) -> stale ts falls to the idle twin. GEAR is NOT imu (Spool OBD derivation, separate producer -- keep it out of states/imu). Raw accel/gyro/mag/temp_c stay on the EDR bus + sensor_schema.py, NOT states/imu

[ATLAS TRANSPORT RULED] the states/imu bridge writes the derived file at ~10-15 Hz latest-wins/lossy (no history on the display path; durable EDR persist stays at the ADR persistHz -- one producer, two cadences); the live card polls states/imu at ~10 Hz off the existing states_http_server (localhost, no-store). Animates the tape+g-trail smoothly with NO new transport. A full SSE/stream is the future EDR-bus target, NOT required here -- do not block on it

stories.title: System-Status 'N ISSUE' drill-down overlay

grounding: NO new numbers introduced. This story adds NO threshold, interval or tuning value -- the rows read the levels the SHIPPED tile builders already computed (obdLinkTile/syncTile/powerTile/driveTile, unedited), and the ordering reuses the shipped SYS_LEVEL_RANK severity map (US-489). Nothing Rex-derived.

The listing floor SYS_ROW_FLOOR = SYS_LEVEL_RANK.unavailable is a re-use of the existing rank vocabulary, not a new constant value; the 'neutral is nominal, not broken' rule it encodes is quoted verbatim from the shipped SYS_LEVEL_RANK comment (US-489).
'seen Ns ago' is the SHIPPED seenDetail() wording (carousel.js, US-400) reused verbatim -- the drill-down does not invent a second freshness phrasing.
Row/overlay copy ('worst-first', 'Back', label + chip + reason + freshness) is verbatim from the US-509 acceptance criteria (Iris CIO-locked F-124 spec 2026-07-31, PM-groomed).

Overlay CSS carries no colour literals: every colour is an existing var(--token) from specs/UI/tokens.css, and the amber-not-red chip ramp mirrors the TD-067/US-488 ruling already applied to the summary line and tile dots.

stories.completionNotes: commit 883477b (impl+tests) + the doc/state commit that follows. SURFACE: the US-489 'SYSTEM . N ISSUE' line is now a gated tap target -> #sys-detail, an overlay of worst-first rows (label + state chip + the tile's own reason + freshness) with a '<- Back'. The rows travel on systemStatusView().drill, so ONE read of the state file feeds the grid, the summary AND the overlay -- the drill-down is structurally incapable of contradicting the card behind it, and no source state is recomputed (AC-4). FOUR HONESTY DECISIONS, EACH PINNED + MUTATION-PROVEN: (1) THE LISTING FLOOR IS 'unavailable', NOT 'amber' -- and this is the one judgement call in the story, so PM please read it: 'ok' is never listed (a green source in a fault list is a FABRICATED fault) and 'neutral' is not listed either, because the shipped SYS_LEVEL_RANK comment documents DRIVE=IDLE as 'nominal but inactive, NOT broken' -- listing it would report a fault in the commonest state there is (key on, no drive started), which is crying wolf. But a known-UNKNOWN IS listed, because the summary line itself reads 'SYSTEM . N UNAVAILABLE' in that state and excluding unavailables would make a tappable headline open an EMPTY overlay -- the exact dead end the story's own goal statement says to remove. Consequence PM should be aware of: in a mixed state the headline counts ISSUES (amber/down) while the list also carries unavailables, so the row count can exceed N. I judged a visible known-unknown better than a hidden one and made the overlay HEAD repeat the tapped line VERBATIM rather than recount it, so the two can never disagree in words. Say if you want them forced equal instead. (2) FRESHNESS IS NEVER FABRICATED -- only obdLink publishes lastSeenS (verified against system_status_emitter.py: sync/power/drive have no age field at all), so those rows read 'age not reported', NOT 'seen 0s ago', which would claim we had just seen a source we never timed. Same lie as US-508's zeroed altitude, different costume. (3) THE AFFORDANCE IS GATED on drill.tappable, so a healthy card never advertises detail it does not have (the validationCriteria's 'not a misleading tap target'). (4) AN OPEN OVERLAY REPAINTS EVERY POLL rather than freezing on the snapshot that opened it -- a frozen age readout is the same fabrication guarded against for the g-dot (US-497) and the rotate bar (US-506); when the last fault clears while the overlay is open it says 'all sources OK' rather than showing an empty box or yanking itself shut. REUSE, NOT A SECOND LANGUAGE: the overlay inherits the US-406 per-code detail shell (.detail-head/.detail-body/.detail-card, the same '<- Back') -- two drill-downs that LOOK different teach the operator two interactions for one idea. AUTO-ROTATE PAUSE (AC-2) needed NO new code: US-506 hung pause on ONE document-level pointerdown precisely so overlay #7 could not forget, so I pinned that seam instead of adding a call site. TDD: 26 of 27 tests proven RED first. The 27th (the pause seam) is a guard on INHERITED behaviour and passed immediately, which proves nothing -- so I mutation-proved it and 4 more (stripped the pause call / fabricated a zero age / lowered the floor to neutral / made the summary always tappable / forked a raw hex into the overlay CSS); all 5 went RED naming the right test. Mutations were run AFTER committing the green work and restored with `git checkout`, so the recovery could not lose the thing it recovered; tree verified identical to HEAD by `git diff --stat` before continuing. GREEN in-loop (synchronous): tests/ui + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 491 passed in 129s; tests/pi/splash = 179 passed / 1 skipped; the story suite 27 passed; ruff clean on the one touched .py. GOTCHA WORTH THE PM'S EYE: passing `-q` on the command line ON TOP of the `-q` already in pyproject addopts makes `-qq`, which SUPPRESSES pytest's summary line entirely -- I read dots-only output twice before noticing. A gate whose summary line you never actually see is not a gate that was read. HOST GAPS unchanged (Sprints 64-68): make/black/mypy absent on this Windows box -- NO .py production code changed by this story, so mypy risk is nil. ARCHITECTURE DoD MET IN-SPRINT: the F-092 System Status section gained a 'Summary drill-down (US-509)' subsection recording all four decisions. ON-PI GATE OWED (A-16, cannot be discharged here): with one source degraded, tap the SYSTEM line -> worst-first list with reason + freshness + Back; with all sources good -> the line is not a tap target. WATCH: (1) #sys-detail shares z-index 45 with #dtc-detail -- they are opened from different cards and never both, but confirm a live DTC takeover still wins the screen. (2) Confirm the chevron does not crowd the summary detail text on the real 480x320 panel (both sit right-aligned; the CSS gives the detail margin-left:auto ahead of it).

stories.completionNotes: commit d5ee7b7. >>> passes:false ON PURPOSE, AND THE REASON IS NARROW -- please read the first paragraph before re-planning. A-1 and A-2 shipped COMPLETE and green; A-3 shipped its structural half. What is missing is ONE external asset: the inlined @font-face woff2. AC A-3 requires it in so many words ('inlined @font-face woff2 data-URI'), and it does not exist -- verified, not assumed: a repo-wide search for *.woff/*.woff2/*.ttf/*.otf returns only specs/samples/Race Sport.ttf (unrelated), there is no @font-face anywhere in specs/UI/**, and Marcus's own groom note to Iris says 'When you have the woff2 base64 for --font-display, drop it and I'll make sure US-510 picks it up.' The locked face is Bahnschrift, which is Microsoft-bundled (not redistributable) and absent from Raspberry Pi OS, so naming it does not put it on the panel. I did not fabricate font base64 and did not substitute a face -- that is a CIO pick in Iris's lane. Filed BL-027 with a ~30-minute fast-follow recipe (the seam is built; it is a payload drop). PM DECISION OWED: close US-510 as-is with A-3 carried (the story's own conditionalOutcomes already prefers shipping ungated fidelity over blocking), or hold it open until Iris drops the base64. >>> WHAT SHIPPED. I chose named tokens over Iris's offered color-mix() DELIBERATELY: a computed mix yields a DIFFERENT colour, which is a restyle wearing a tokenization's clothes, and Atlas made 'a diff that moves a rendered pixel FAILS' the gate for this whole story. Rather than leave a silent gap I bounded it: the whole-file guard allows EXACTLY short-form #fff/#000 and nothing else, and long-form #000000 is separately forbidden outside :root (that value is --bg's job now), so the debt cannot grow by one character. stories.title: Debounced 'parked' signal for the kebab (stop the OBD-blip flicker)

grounding: parkedOnS=8 / parkedOffS=3 are BOTH verbatim from the US-511 acceptance criteria (Iris CIO-locked F-124 spec 2026-07-31, PM-groomed). Neither is Rex-derived, and no third threshold was invented.

The display-side-debounce choice over an emitter field is AC-3 verbatim ('NEAR-TERM = display-side debounce of the idle it already consumes -- NO new contract (Iris's recommendation)... default to display-debounce now'). The emitter path is explicitly NOT taken -- it needs the Atlas nod the AC names.

pi.display.carousel.* as the config home + resolveCarouselConfig's positive-only rule are REUSE of the shipped US-506 seam, not a new mechanism. No new placeholder, no new loader, no server key list (verified: _loadDisplaySection passes the section wholesale).
carouselIdle's strict `idle === true` read is UNCHANGED (Atlas idle-SSOT b) -- this story debounces its output, it does not touch how the flag is read.

stories.completionNotes: commit b359f62. SHAPE: a pure reducer parkedInit()/parkedNext(prev, rawIdle, nowMs, cfg) -> {parked, raw, sinceMs} sits between carouselIdle and the menu policy; the clock arrives as an argument like every other US-506 predicate, so the whole debounce is node-testable with no timer of its own. Thresholds asymmetric as specified: slow to OFFER a single tap into a service stop (8 s), fast to WITHDRAW it once the car moves (3 s) -- pinned BEHAVIOURALLY, not as a comparison of two constants. >>> THE ONE STRUCTURAL DECISION FOR THE PM'S EYE: I CHANGED menuAccess's SIGNATURE. It took the system-status payload and called carouselIdle on it -- i.e. it did its own ACQUISITION -- so a debounce placed upstream would have been bypassable by the next edit for free; AC-2 says the kebab keys off 'parked' NOT raw idle, and the only way to make that hold is to put the raw flag OUT OF REACH. menuAccess(parked) now applies policy only (the standing SSOT directive). This creates a footgun and I closed it: an un-migrated caller would hand it an OBJECT, and a truthy test would read that as parked FOREVER -- the kebab pinned on screen at 70 mph, the exact hazard US-490 exists to prevent -- so the test is a strict `parked === true` and a raw payload fails CLOSED. Pinned + mutation-proved. >>> THREE HONESTY GUARDS ON THE DERIVED HOLD, each mutation-proved: (1) RE-ANCHOR, DON'T ACCUMULATE -- every change of reading restarts the run, so six 2 s blips never sum to one 3 s run; an accumulator would keep the flicker and merely delay it. (2) AN UNMEASURED HOLD IS NOT A HOLD -- an unreadable clock returns the state COMPLETELY untouched, including the reading; recording a reading without a timestamp would let the next real clock credit this run's elapsed time to the PREVIOUS reading, a fabricated hold assembled from two halves. (3) A NEGATIVE hold (NTP step back -- this Pi has no RTC) re-anchors rather than stranding the signal for the size of the step; on the OFF edge stranding means the kebab stays up while the car drives away. >>> TDD: 28 of 30 tests proven RED first (the 2 first-run greens were guards on inherited behaviour). After committing the green work I MUTATION-PROVED 7 defects -- kebab always visible / long-press override gated / debounce bypassed (the original defect re-inserted) / hold reset every tick / accumulate-not-re-anchor / negative-hold guard dropped / the loose body slicer -- ALL 7 went RED naming the right test, and `git diff --stat` on the two mutated files was EMPTY afterwards. M4 is the one I most wanted proven: initialising the state inside updateMenuAccess leaves every pure test green while the kebab NEVER APPEARS, because a hold that resets every 250 ms can never reach 8 s. >>> TWO PRE-EXISTING PINS RE-AIMED, both overturned on purpose (the US-506 rule: an overturned test is evidence, not an obstacle). test_carousel_menu_access.py's six menuAccess fixtures could no longer reach the function, so they are re-aimed one link UPSTREAM at carouselIdle -- the invariant they were really guarding (idle is read from the SSOT, never the drive-state string, and fails closed on every unreadable variant) is unchanged and still on this path. And test_pollAppliesMenuAccessEveryTick's expected call text moved to `updateMenuAccess(sysData, nowMs)`; the invariant (applied every tick) is unchanged. Nothing was deleted or softened. >>> TEST-HARNESS FLAG WORTH ROUTING: my own absence pin ('carouselIdle' not in menuAccess's body) went RED against CORRECT code -- FOURTH occurrence of the family (US-507, US-509). The cause this time is new and is in a helper I COPIED from tests/ui/test_carousel_nav_model.py: its _fnBody slices 'up to the next function declaration' at a FIXED 4-space indent, but carousel.js declares pure logic at 2-space and browser helpers at 4, so a 2-space function's 'body' ran on through everything up to the DOM block -- and swallowed the comment that DOCUMENTS the identifier the test forbids. I fixed MY copy to be indent-aware (cuts at the function's OWN closing brace) and pinned the slicer itself at both edges, because over-stripping is the dangerous direction: a slice cut to nothing makes an absence assertion pass VACUOUSLY. PM: the loose helper is still in test_carousel_nav_model.py (and a similar fixed-terminator one in test_carousel_menu_access.py). I did NOT touch them -- scope fence, and no defect is demonstrated there -- but any absence assertion they feed is over-broad and any presence assertion is at vacuity risk. Worth a housekeeping sweep. >>> SCOPE FENCE HELD: updateHomeNav still edge-triggers on RAW carouselIdle. AC-2 names the kebab only, and the home-slot swap is a different fact with a different tolerance (a nav jump wants the real edge, not a delayed one). Not changed, flagged here rather than silently widened. GREEN in-loop (synchronous): tests/ui + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 549 passed exit 0; tests/pi/splash = 179 passed / 1 skipped; the story suite 30 passed; ruff clean on both touched .py; python validate_config.py passes. HOST GAPS unchanged (Sprints 64-68): make/black/mypy absent on this Windows box -- states_http_server.py changed by a DOCSTRING ONLY (no signature, no logic), so mypy risk is nil, but PM please still run it at integration since US-508 changed imu_state_bridge.py + validator.py earlier this sprint. (2) Confirm the long-press override still opens the menu during the 8 s window, since that is what makes the slower affordance safe.
